Samir — thanks for flagging this and for sending the forwarded ICS. I can confirm we saw the same mismatch when the APAC PM forwarded it: GCal interpreted the event as floating (no TZ id) so it anchored to the recipient's calendar zone when forwarded.

Quick notes / proposal:
- We should avoid relying on forwarded ICS files for cross-region invites: they can drop VTIMEZONE or the TZID attribute and then \"float.\"
- I'll put a hard UTC time in the subject + include a concrete timezone label (e.g., \"2027-08-03 10:00 UTC / 11:00 BST / 18:00 SGT\") to reduce ambiguity.
- Proposed: Wed Aug 4 at 01:00 UTC (which is 02:00 BST / 09:00 SGT). If that slot doesn't work for EMEA, we can take Tue Aug 3 10:00 UTC (11:00 BST). Either way, I'll send a fresh invite from Redwood with a Google Meet link and explicit times.

Can you confirm which of the two slots works for the broader group? I'll avoid forwarding any APAC-local invites and send a new canonical invite instead.

Thanks,

Agree — we've seen this a few times with partner-forwarded invites. Two operational fixes that help immediately:
- Send the invite from the organizing calendar (not forwarding) so Google preserves the VTIMEZONE / TZID.
- Add an explicit UTC anchor in the subject line and in the first sentence of the event body. Example subject: \"Redwood demo — Aug 03 2027, 10:00 UTC | 11:00 BST | 18:00 SGT\".

I'll create the canonical Redwood invite for Tue Aug 3 10:00 UTC (our recommended slot) and include a short note in the description: \"If you see a different local time after forwarding, please use the UTC time above.\"
